text.content:
Everything for the one-shot is in the Demo folder of the Compendium Packs tab. The script is the same as the PDF’s; at the table the PDF’s Entity cards and tracker are for players without Foundry, and here the sheets and the Raid HUD do their jobs.

  1. Bring it in. The first time the Storyteller opens a world, the system offers to set it up (or Configure Settings → Set up a ready-made game, tick Lantern Night in Hallowby): the four Demo compendiums come into the world in folders named after them, keeping their IDs (the map’s pins open the script’s pages by them). By hand: right-click each Demo compendium and choose Import All Content, the script and guide first, then the scenes, the Entities and the macro, keeping the documents’ IDs if Foundry asks.
  2. The scenes. Activate The Castle for Part One, then Hallowby for Part Two. Hallowby has no grid: tokens stand anywhere, and every move takes one Turn, so where a token stands only says which place it’s at.
  3. The Entities. When the players have chosen (Part One), give each player Owner of their Entity (right-click the actor, Configure Ownership). Change Castle Duties on the sheets.
  4. Start the raid. Drag the macro Hallowby: Start the Raid to the hotbar and run it: a new Easy raid on The Raid window (the Raid HUD), Suspicion 0, Turn 1, with Hallowby’s list. Run it after the players own their Entities: the raid takes every Entity with a player owner (or tick In this raid on a sheet).
  5. The tokens. Drag each Entity onto Hallowby, onto the yard at The Way Out: the party starts at the edge of town.

• Reading. Open the script journal, or click a pin on the map: each place’s pin opens its page.
  • Rolling. Players click a trait on their sheet. The roll dialog asks for the Mask or the Monster and the Difficulty (read it from the place’s page), offers abilities and friends’ help, and has ticks for Castle Duty, the loud way, watched, the way out, the furniture’s obstacle and the lock-up. Suspicion goes on the HUD by itself.
  • Turns. Next Turn on the HUD at the end of each Turn. After the 12th comes dawn.
  • Tell checks and crowds. Tell check when the script says to make one; Group check before two or more roll the florist’s crowd in one Turn.
  • Chases. Trouble at a watched obstacle opens The Chase tracker for everyone; the final flight runs on it too. Captures show on the HUD at the lock-up.
  • The end. When the party is out, How the year went on the card gives the result and the epilogue; Part Three of the script says the same words.
  • By hand. Every automation has a switch in Configure Settings, and the HUD has Suspicion and Turn buttons for anything the dice didn’t do.
